title: I am, you are, it is

sections.title: What you will learn to say

blocks.text: In this lesson you learn to talk about yourself, the person in front of you, other people and things: «I am ready», «you are right», «she is upstairs», «it is heavy». Every one of these sentences has a small word in the middle: am, is or are.

examples.translation: You agree with the other person.
She is on a higher floor.

blocks.text: Think of am, is and are as clips. They don't add meaning, but without them the sentence falls apart.
Almost every sentence in this lesson is built the same way: first who or what, then am, is or are, then a word about them: where they are, what they are like, how they feel.

drill.why: When you talk about yourself, I always goes with am.

sections.title: I am — when you talk about yourself

blocks.text: About yourself, it is always I am. In many languages you can say «I tired» or just «tired». In English that sounds broken. Say the full thing: I am tired.

examples.translation: I don't know where I am.
It is my first day here.
I got back to my home.

blocks.text: I is always a capital letter, even in the middle of a sentence.
To say «not», put not right after am, is or are: I am not hungry. Don't use no here. I no cold sounds broken; I am not cold is fine.

examples.translation: The room is fine for me.

drill.hint: One word is wrong here. Tap it.
drill.fix: After am you need not, not no: I am not cold.

sections.title: You are — when you talk to someone

blocks.text: When you tell a person something about them, use you are. English has only one you: for a friend, for your boss, and for a whole group. After you, it is always are.

drill.question: You want to tell someone they are right. Which is correct?
drill.explain: After you it is always are, for one person or many.

sections.title: He is, she is — when you talk about another person

blocks.text: For a man, say he. For a woman, say she. After both, use is. You use them when you talk about a person, not to them: «he is tall», «she is upstairs».

examples.translation: She is on a higher floor.

blocks.text: You are kind — you say it to the person. He is kind — you tell someone else about him.

sections.title: It is — for a thing, a place or the weather

blocks.text: For a thing, a room, a door or the weather, use it is. Many languages just say «Cold» or «Open». English needs a start: It is cold, It is open. Is cold on its own is not a full sentence.

sections.title: We are, they are — for more than one

blocks.text: For you and other people together, say we are. For other people or for several things, say they are. After we and they it is always are, however many there are.

examples.translation: The new shoes are too small.

blocks.text: They is for people and for things. You can say They are tight about new shoes.

sections.title: Who — and which clip goes with them

blocks.text: The whole lesson fits into one short table. If you're not sure, first find who the sentence is about, then take their clip.

drill.why: After they it is always are.

drill.prompt: She isn't downstairs. Say where she is.

blocks.text: When people speak, they almost always shorten the clip: I'm for I am, it's for it is. Same meaning, just faster. The ' shows where letters are missing.
Both forms are correct. The short one sounds more natural when you talk; the full one sounds firmer.

sections.title: Where you are: home, inside, upstairs — no extra words

blocks.text: The clip also works for places: I am home, she is upstairs. With here, home, back, inside, outside, upstairs and nearby you don't need any other word. I am in home sounds wrong.

examples.translation: I got back to my home.
She is on a higher floor.

sections.title: Feelings use am, is, are too

blocks.text: In many languages you «have» cold or hunger, or the cold is «to you». English just uses the clip: I am cold, I am hungry, I am sorry. Learn these as whole phrases.

examples.translation: I want to open the window.

blocks.text: Almost all of these come down to two things: the clip is missing, or it's the wrong one. Check: who is the sentence about, and which clip goes with them?

drill.why: After we it is always are, and not doesn't change that.

blocks.text: One pattern for the whole lesson: who + am / is / are + a word about them. Never skip the clip. To say «not», put not after it. When you talk, shorten it: I'm, it's, they're.
